note: No .env file is committed. No SQL schema, migrations or RLS policies are in the repo, and CLAUDE.md line 42 says there is no RLS and no rate limiting. The model is called only from the Python backend, so there is no ai_browser_call. Live (streaming) mode is the UI default and it skips the email, memory and emergency-log steps that /book runs. Root App.jsx is an older copy of the UI that the Vite app does not import. INTEGRATION.md still tells people to copy it. | Second labeler: No database schema or migrations are committed, so the database_rules labels are inferred from code and from CLAUDE.md line 42, which says there is no RLS. No ai_browser_call found. All model calls run in the Python backend. No real secret values are committed. .env.example holds placeholders only. The root App.jsx is an older copy that the Vite app does not import. Cancel booking checks ownership and admin stats checks is_admin on the server, so those are fine.

labels.what: book_slot marks the slot taken and inserts the appointment straight from the model call. The system prompt tells the model to pick and book without asking the user which option they want. There is no confirm step.
emergency_book books the next slot and flags it as priority straight from the model call. The emergency prompt forbids clarifying questions, so nobody confirms before the booking.
The book_slot description says to call it only after the user confirmed. book_slot has no confirmation check, and the system prompt at prompts.py 37-40 tells the model the opposite.

Rule: use emergency_book only for a medical emergency (also in the tool description at tools.py 103-108). emergency_book is offered on every turn, and the code never checks that emergency mode was detected. Any turn can create a priority booking.
Rule: do not book without the patient name. book_slot accepts any string, including an empty one, and never ties the name to the logged-in user.

Rule: never invent IDs and only use IDs from earlier tool results. execute_tool passes any doctor_id or patient_id straight to the database. The model-supplied patient_id is saved on the appointment with no check (db.py 186).

book_slot checks that the slot exists and is free. It has no limit on bookings per user or session, no check that the date is in the future, and accepts anonymous callers (user_id None). Anonymous bookings hold slots that no one can cancel.
emergency_book has no limit or validation. A loop or repeated messages can flag many priority bookings.

Booking reads the whole slots JSON array, flips one flag in Python and writes the array back with no lock or conditional update. Two bookings on the same doctor and day can overwrite each other, so a booked slot can show as free again. cancel_booking at 331-344 has the same pattern. The duplicate fallback at 195-214 relies on a unique constraint that is not in the repo.
send_notification prints to the server log and returns success with a timestamp. The step label says Confirmation sent and the detail says delivered (tools.py 298, 326-327).
resolve_location reads a hardcoded table of 12 city coordinates. It is a stand-in for geocoding, and any other place returns nothing.

In Live mode (the default, line 78) the card shows Confirmation email sent (1001-1005) once the stub send_notification step completes. /api/chat/stream never calls _send_confirmation_email, so no email goes out. That path also skips the patient memory save and the emergency log.

mark_emergency_booking only appends to an in-memory list and prints. The comment says production would notify on-call staff, but nobody is notified and the log is lost on restart. The emergency prompt makes the model tell the patient it overrode the queue, yet the only effect is is_emergency true on the row.

If the provider import fails, the server silently switches to the mock agent. The UI then shows an Appointment confirmed card for a booking that does not exist. Only a small header pill says mock mode.
Canned mock agent run with fixed doctors, Dr. Ananya Sharma at Sunrise Skin Clinic, and a fixed date of 2026-07-07, returned in the same shape as a real booking.

The seeder writes generated doctors with random names, ratings from 3.5 to 5.0 and random experience into the live database. It attaches them to real hospital brands such as Apollo, Fortis and Manipal. The prompt says it searches the real database, and the README says this is not placeholder data.
Queue wait times and waiting counts are random numbers seeded once. Nothing updates them, yet the prompt, the tool output and the UI present them as live wait times.
Landing page demo animation with hardcoded steps and a hardcoded confirmed booking for Dr. Ananya Sharma (lines 293-296). It is marketing, but it shows email delivered as a done step.
Schedules are seeded only for 2026-07-12 to 2026-07-19. Slot search looks at today plus 4 days, so after 2026-07-19 every search finds no slots.

The quick-book SPECIALTIES list claims to match the seed data. It has General Physician where the seed has General Medicine, and it leaves out Psychiatry. Quick-booking General Physician finds no doctors.

Old root UI copy also falls back to http://localhost:8000.
CORS has the production origin hardcoded and allows any localhost port with credentials in every environment.
The server port is 8000 in app.py and in the UI default, but the Procfile starts uvicorn on 8080. The same setting has two different values.
MAX_STEPS 8 is a hand copy of MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS, which is defined separately in three provider files. Step ids count tool calls, not rounds, so the panel can show a step number above 8 of 8.
The Claude model id is hardcoded in code. OpenRouter and Ollama read theirs from env vars.
/book needs no login. user_id is optional, and the comment at line 596 says auth does not gate booking. Anyone can run the agent and write real appointments.
/api/chat/stream, the default UI path, needs no login either. user_id is optional, so anonymous callers can run the agent and book.
/emergency reads no auth header at all. Anyone can trigger priority bookings and confirmation emails under any patient name.
The /ws/{session_id} websocket runs the agent and books with no auth. The session id comes from the URL.
/memory/save and /memory/{patient_name} need no login. Anyone can read or overwrite any patient's stored preferences and booking history by name.
/emergency/log is open. It returns every emergency booking with patient-related text and the full user message as the reason, which can include symptoms.
Conversation sessions are keyed by a client-supplied id built from a timestamp, with no owner check. Anyone who sends another user's session id continues that conversation with its history.
The find_patient_by_name tool returns the first patient record that partly matches any name, with no scoping to the logged-in user.
The admin check for the live booking feed runs only in browser code. The realtime subscription then uses the public anon key, which does not depend on admin status.

The repo states there is no RLS, and no policies exist in the repo. The anon key ships to the browser, so tables such as users (with password_hash), appointments, patients and cancellations may be readable or writable through the Supabase REST API.
The browser subscribes to appointments changes with the anon key. This works only if the anon role can read appointments, so patient names and bookings are open to anyone holding the public key.
The Supabase anon key is read from VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY and shipped to the browser. It is public by design.
Hardcoded fallback JWT signing secret, secret value present. If JWT_SECRET is unset, anyone can forge tokens for any user id, including an admin's id, because the admin check trusts the token sub.
The session JWT is stored in localStorage. It lasts 30 days with no revocation.
There is no rate limit on any paid model endpoint (/book, /api/chat/stream, /emergency, /ws), and most need no login. Anyone can spend the Claude or OpenRouter credits.

Stored prompt injection. Unauthenticated /memory/save stores notes and a preferred hospital for any name. get_context_for_agent pastes them into the system prompt for every later request that uses that name (app.py 315-324), with no guard.
Confirmation emails go to whatever address the request sends, with no login or ownership check. Anonymous callers can make the service send mail to anyone.
Old root UI copy has a sign-in screen where the password is never checked. The user object exists only in browser state.
book_slot writes an appointment and locks the slot straight from the model call. The system prompt tells the model to pick and book without asking the user, so no person approves the booking
emergency_book books a priority slot that jumps the queue with no staff or patient approval. The emergency prompt also says do not ask questions, act now

The only instruction to tell a patient to call emergency services or go to the ER is in the prompt. The /emergency and /book handlers return the model reply as is, with no fixed safety message added in code
Mock run_agent returns canned tool steps and a canned booking for Dr. Ananya Sharma at Sunrise Skin Clinic on 2026-07-07. It runs when USE_MOCK_AGENT is true or when the provider import fails

Appointment card shows Confirmation email sent when the send_notification step completes. That tool only prints a log line, and the default live-stream path never sends the email, so the user sees a confirmation that did not happen

The streaming endpoint, which the UI uses by default (liveMode true), books the slot but never calls _send_confirmation_email or mark_emergency_booking. Only POST /book does. README says every booking sends a real email
Timeline label says Confirmation sent and detail says delivered for the send_notification stub, which sends nothing
Every query, including user-facing ones, uses the service role key. CLAUDE.md says there is no RLS, so each ownership rule lives only in Python filters
Patient name and free-text notes from the unauthenticated /memory/save endpoint are pasted into the system prompt with no guard. Anyone can plant instructions for a named patient's future sessions
Confirmation email goes to whatever patient_email the request sends, with no verification and no login. Anyone can make the server email any address
Emergency mode turns on by keyword match, including bare urgent and emergency. Any user can type urgent to get queue-jumping priority bookings
SESSIONS and patient memory are process dicts with no expiry or size cap. Memory grows with each new session id and all data is lost on restart
Login has no attempt limit or lockout, so passwords can be brute forced
CORS allows credentials from any localhost port in production, with all methods and headers
find_doctors caps rows at 25 before the distance filter, so near doctors can be cut off. Slot lookahead is 4 days at line 107 and 7 days at line 201, two values for the same kind of window
JWT expiry fixed at 30 days in code
